header:
Date: 2027-02-03
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Tariq Singh (Redwood SE), Becky Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Argosy), Ravi Patel (Argosy), Sofia Romero (Argosy CISO)
summary: Follow-up to the Jan 25th incident where Argosy experienced intermittent spike in inference latency and 502s during peak ETL window. Redwood reviewed initial RCA, discussed mitigations (KV cache tuning, autoscaler safeguards, graceful fallbacks to smaller variants), agreed on reproduction plan and next steps for security/audit deliverables.
topics: KV cache eviction pattern and reproduction plan
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, this is the Argosy postmortem follow-up, i'll kick off \u0014 we have tariq from se and becky on csm. good to see you maya, ravi, sofia.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Thanks Lena, appreciate the quick turnaround. we had a repeat of higher p50 and p95 last week same pattern as before, so keen to walk the fixes.
[00:31] Tariq Singh: quick note \u0014 first we went through the timeline; on Jan 25th there was a burst from the nightly ETL that increased concurrency from ~150 to ~800 over 10 minutes, prefix cache hit dropped and then kv cache got evicted when memory pressure spiked, which caused longer token decode times and some request timeouts.
[00:55] Ravi Patel: yeah that's what we saw, our app hit >500ms token latencies and eventually some 502s. question \u0014 was the eviction due to a bug or expected under pressure?
[01:10] Tariq Singh: initial root cause is interplay of autoscaler and continuous batching. the GPU serving pods used a shared in-memory kv cache with an LRU; under sudden concurrency the memory footprint grew more than expected because of longer sequence lengths hitting the cache, and the eviction threshold kicked in. when eviction happened, a lot of requests couldn't use the warm kv cache and cold-start token generation took much longer.
[01:40] Sofia Romero: is there an option to persist the cache to disk or external store? for compliance we also want to avoid unexpected in-memory retention, and need clear audit logs.
[01:52] Tariq Singh: persisting the full kv cache to disk isn't something we'd recommend for latency-sensitive inference \u0014 disk IO kills token latency. what we can do: prioritized eviction, reserve a pinned cache portion for critical routes, and add a fast warm-up strategy (small prefetch), plus explicit autoscaler safety thresholds so we don't scale down during sudden bursts.
[02:16] Becky Ruiz: also we proposed a fallthrough model routing policy \u0014 if the primary variant exceeds latency SLOs we fall back to a smaller quantized variant automatically so user traffic still gets responses albeit slightly different quality. Argosy had asked about quality regressions earlier.
[02:34] Maya Chen: Concern here is correctness for clinical summaries; fallback is acceptable if we can flag outputs and keep audit trail. sofia, thoughts?
[02:44] Sofia Romero: flagged outputs + metadata + full audit for each inference is ok. we need retention window and proof of KMS usage.
[02:51] Lena Ortiz: point taken \u0014 we'll include KMS key rotation logs and audit export in the package.
[03:00] Ravi Patel: there was also mention in the postmortem about a misconfigured burst policy on the dedicated pool \u0014 can you recap?
[03:08] Tariq Singh: yes, autoscaler policy had a 2-minute cooldown which allowed simultaneous pod evictions during a scale-down event triggered by a previous spike; combined with the batcher health check lag, some pods were marked unhealthy and took time to recover. we've proposed lowering cooldowns and adding a pre-scale drain that writes cache state to a warmup buffer and also marking critical pods as nondrainable during maintenance windows.
[03:36] Maya Chen: is nondrainable supported for our dedicated capacity? we'll need that for our nightly ETL window.
[03:42] Tariq Singh: yes, we can pin a % of the pool \u0014 for example reserve 20% non-drain \u0014 and we can expose that as a policy you can configure in the Console.
[03:50] Ravi Patel: can we see simulated runs? we would like a bench (latency/cost) with our traffic profile.
[03:56] Lena Ortiz: absolutely; next week SE will run bench with sample traces you share, and we'll iterate on batching/quantization to meet p95 300ms target.
[04:05] Maya Chen: On security: we received the preliminary SOC2 evidence but need deeper artifacts \u0014 audit log exports, sso logs, and the incident timeline sanitized.
[04:15] Becky Ruiz: we'll send the sanitized timeline today and the audit log export within 72 hours. for KMS details we'll include key usage and rotation policy doc.
[04:25] Sofia Romero: one more \u0014 encryption in transit and at rest, do you store any customer data in logs that could be sensitive?
[04:32] Lena Ortiz: logs are scrubbed by default; we have an option to disable PII capture and we can provide a SOC2 coverage mapping.
[04:40] Ravi Patel: earlier you mentioned fallback to smaller model \u0014 what's the expected token cost delta? we need ROI for cost vs latency.
[04:49] Tariq Singh: rough estimate \u0014 primary model costs ~3x per-token of the quantized fallback. but because of batching and cache hit improvements the per-request cost can drop by ~60% if cache stabilizes. we'll include detailed numbers in the bench report.
[05:05] Maya Chen: ok, action items recap - tariq reproduce cache eviction in staging and dump traces, lena send timeline and docs, ravi share traffic profile.
[05:16] Becky Ruiz: we'll schedule the bench and also propose a canary roll plan so you can test fallback without impacting prod.
[05:22] Lena Ortiz: any blockers for the plan?
[05:26] Sofia Romero: just timing \u0014 we need the audits before we agree to any non-prod data movement.
[05:31] Lena Ortiz: understood \u0014 we'll prioritize sanitized logs and the SOC2 mapping.
[05:35] Ravi Patel: one nit \u0014 the transcript from your earlier postmortem had a couple of product-name OCR issues, said \u0018Redwood Dedicated\u0019 as \u0018Redwood Delete\u0019 in places, small thing but confusing for our legal team.
[05:47] Tariq Singh: oh, thanks \u0014 we'll correct that in the docs we send.
[05:52] Lena Ortiz: great; last thing, we'll put an explicit SLA for latency on the canary and rollback conditions. everyone ok with the next steps?
[05:59] Maya Chen: yes. thanks all.

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-hearings (product names), filler words and overlapping talk. Links shared during the call: incident timeline doc (link), SOC2 evidence packet (link), bench spreadsheet (link).
